evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/saved_search_alerts.rs:197-240 (run_once matching loop) advances each saved search's watermark UNCONDITIONALLY after a capped scan, so any match beyond the cap in that cadence window is permanently dropped. The scan is `find_new_match_listing_ids(&query, Some(since), self.config.match_limit)` where match_limit defaults to 100 (SavedSearchAlertConfig::default, :80). Its SQL (crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/searches.rs:68-104) is `... WHERE l.published_at > $12 ORDER BY l.published_at DESC LIMIT $13` — it returns only the NEWEST match_limit listings published since the watermark.

After the capped scan the worker calls `mark_saved_search_matched(&mut *conn, search.id, ids.len())` (saved_search_alerts.rs:237-240), and that repo fn sets `last_matched_at = now()` UNCONDITIONALLY (searches.rs:134-159, `SET last_matched_at = now()`). It takes no timestamp argument, so the watermark always jumps to the wall clock, never to the oldest listing actually processed. Consequence: if more than match_limit (100) listings match a saved search within one cadence window — entirely plausible for a broad daily/weekly search such as 'flats in Bratislava' after a bulk portal import — the query keeps the newest 100 (DESC), the watermark leaps to now(), and every OLDER matching listing in that window is skipped forever. Because ORDER BY is `published_at DESC`, the dropped rows are precisely the OLDEST matches (the ones that have waited longest), and the next run resumes from `published_at > now()` so they can never be re-selected. There is no continuation cursor and no carry-over.

This silently defeats the feature's stated purpose ('new listing matches your search -> you're notified', header doc :1-17) under exactly the high-volume conditions where alerts matter most, with no error and no log — the user simply never receives alerts for the majority of a large batch. Fix options (all local to this worker + repo): (a) advance the watermark to the MIN published_at of the returned ids minus epsilon (resume-from-oldest) so the next due run drains the remainder instead of skipping it; or (b) loop find_new_match_listing_ids page-by-page until fewer than match_limit rows come back before advancing to now(); or (c) at minimum emit a tracing::warn when ids.len() == match_limit so the truncation is observable. Confidence medium: the DESC+LIMIT query and the unconditional now() watermark are both confirmed in source and the full path from run_once -> query -> watermark is traced; the >100-per-window trigger depends on listing volume rather than being unconditionally reachable, so not upgraded to high.
